source: General telecom industry knowledge (eTOM process areas, TMF Open API concepts, 3GPP and EU regulatory basics). Written for the demo; no customer data. TMF API numbers and regulatory statements are curated and need review by a domain expert.

nordwave.label: Customer
nordwave.description: The person or business that buys from the operator and is responsible for paying. One customer can hold several subscriptions.

telco.why: Every agent action is about a customer; consent, segment and billing account all hang off this record, so agents must never mix up customer and subscription.

nordwave.label: Subscription
nordwave.description: A customer's running instance of an offer, for example one mobile line on a plan. It carries the phone number, the price in force and the contract.

telco.why: Questions like 'what am I paying for?' are answered at subscription level, not at offer level: two customers on the same offer can have different prices.

nordwave.label: Customer segment
nordwave.description: A group of customers treated alike for pricing and campaigns, for example consumer, small business, high-value or at-risk.

telco.why: Offers, retention rules and credit limits usually differ by segment, so an agent needs the segment before it proposes anything.

nordwave.label: ARPU
nordwave.description: Average revenue per user: total revenue in a period divided by the average number of users. The operator's standard yardstick for how much a customer is worth each month.

telco.why: A retention offer that cuts ARPU may still be right if it avoids a lost customer; agents need ARPU to show that trade-off.

nordwave.label: Customer lifetime value
nordwave.description: The margin an operator expects to earn from a customer over the whole relationship, discounted to today.

telco.why: It sets how much an operator should spend to keep a customer: a credit or discount is worth giving only when it is smaller than the value it protects.

nordwave.label: Promotion
nordwave.description: A time-limited commercial incentive, such as a price reduction or free months, applied on top of a normal offer.

telco.why: Promotions change the price a customer actually pays without changing the catalogue, which is a common reason a bill differs from what the customer expected.

nordwave.label: Eligibility
nordwave.description: The rules that decide whether a customer may buy or switch to an offer, for example a minimum tenure, a credit class or being in a coverage area.

telco.why: An agent that proposes an offer the customer cannot take wastes a conversation and creates a complaint; eligibility is checked before the proposal.

nordwave.label: Next best action
nordwave.description: The single most useful thing to offer or do for a customer right now, chosen from their situation, their eligibility and their consent.

telco.why: It is the decision an agent is usually asked to make. It stays safe only when consent, eligibility and policy are checked first.

nordwave.label: Postpaid
nordwave.description: A plan where the customer uses the service first and receives a bill at the end of each cycle.

telco.why: Postpaid creates credit exposure and bill shock, because the customer finds out the cost after the usage has happened.

nordwave.label: Prepaid
nordwave.description: A plan where the customer pays in advance and usage is deducted from a balance, so the service stops when the balance runs out.

telco.why: Prepaid has no bill, so there is no bill shock, but charging has to react in real time and a wrong deduction is felt immediately.

nordwave.label: Contract
nordwave.description: The agreed terms between operator and customer: the price, the minimum term, notice periods and any device instalments.

telco.why: The contract decides what can change and when. A price rise or an early exit can be allowed or forbidden by it.

nordwave.label: MVNO and wholesale
nordwave.description: A mobile virtual network operator sells mobile service under its own brand over another operator's network and pays wholesale rates for usage.

telco.why: Many ATLAS-style BSS deployments serve MVNOs. The agents must treat the host network's wholesale charges and the retail price as separate things.

nordwave.label: Customer satisfaction
nordwave.description: How happy customers say they are, usually measured with Net Promoter Score (would you recommend us) or CSAT (how was this contact).

telco.why: Satisfaction is the early signal for churn. A resolved case that left the customer angry still counts as a failure.

nordwave.label: Device financing
nordwave.description: Selling a handset on monthly instalments, either bundled in the airtime bill or as a separate credit agreement.

telco.why: Instalments are a large part of a monthly bill and are fixed by the contract. An agent must not offer to waive them as if they were usage.

nordwave.label: MSISDN
nordwave.description: The public telephone number of a subscription, the one customers dial and quote.

telco.why: Customers identify themselves by phone number, but numbers can be ported or reassigned, so it identifies a subscription only at a point in time.

nordwave.label: IMSI
nordwave.description: The international mobile subscriber identity stored on the SIM or eSIM. The network uses it, and the customer never sees it.

telco.why: It links a subscription to a physical or embedded SIM, which is why a SIM swap changes it while the phone number stays the same.

nordwave.label: Billing account
nordwave.description: The record that gathers charges from one or more subscriptions, holds the bill cycle and payment method, and receives the bill.

telco.why: A credit or dispute is applied to a billing account, not to a phone line. Families and businesses often share one.

nordwave.label: Bill cycle
nordwave.description: The recurring period (usually a month) after which usage and fees are totalled into a bill, and the bill run that does it.

telco.why: It decides when a credit appears and when a charge becomes due. Agents promise 'on your next bill' only after checking the cycle date.

nordwave.label: Charging
nordwave.description: Pricing and deducting usage as it happens, using the customer's balance and plan. Known as the online charging system (OCS), or the charging function (CHF) in 5G.

telco.why: It is the only place that can stop a service the moment a limit is hit. Spend caps and prepaid depend on it.

nordwave.label: Rating
nordwave.description: Turning a usage record into money by applying the plan's price, tiers, bundles and discounts.

telco.why: Rating is where a price becomes a charge. The rule in this demo is that no language model computes it; agents read the result.

nordwave.label: Balance
nordwave.description: What a customer has left to use: money on a prepaid account, or the remaining part of a data or minute allowance.

telco.why: 'How much do I have left?' is one of the most common questions. The answer must come from charging, not from an estimate.

nordwave.label: Usage record (CDR)
nordwave.description: A record of one call, text or data session: who, when, how long or how much, and on which network.

telco.why: CDRs are the raw material for rating, billing and revenue assurance. A missing or duplicated one becomes a wrong charge.

nordwave.label: Payment
nordwave.description: Money received from a customer against a bill or a balance, by card, direct debit, bank transfer or voucher.

telco.why: Payment status decides whether dunning starts. A bill showing as unpaid right after a payment is a classic case for care.

nordwave.label: Spend cap
nordwave.description: A limit the customer or the operator sets on spending, after which usage is blocked or needs confirmation.

telco.why: It is the main control against bill shock. In the EU a default cap applies to data roaming unless the customer chooses otherwise.

nordwave.label: Usage alert
nordwave.description: A message sent when usage or spend crosses a threshold, for example 80% of the allowance or a roaming charge limit.

telco.why: Alerts are the cheapest way to prevent a complaint. When one was sent late or never, the customer has a fair claim for a goodwill credit.

nordwave.label: Fair use policy
nordwave.description: A rule that limits or slows heavy use of an 'unlimited' plan so that a few users do not degrade service for everyone.

telco.why: A customer whose speed dropped may have hit fair use rather than a fault. Agents must tell these two cases apart.

nordwave.label: Roaming
nordwave.description: Using the mobile service on a foreign network, which the home operator pays for through a wholesale agreement and passes on to the customer.

telco.why: Roaming is the largest single source of bill shock, because rates and rules depend on the country and the plan.

nordwave.label: Inter-operator settlement
nordwave.description: The exchange of usage records and payments between operators for roaming, interconnect and wholesale services.

telco.why: Roaming charges can arrive days after the usage. That delay is why a bill can contain a charge the customer cannot remember.

nordwave.label: Revenue assurance
nordwave.description: The discipline of checking that everything the network delivered is rated, billed and collected, and that nothing is billed wrongly.

telco.why: It finds the errors that cause leakage and overbilling. A pattern of care credits often points to a revenue assurance defect.

nordwave.label: Order to cash
nordwave.description: The whole path from a customer ordering, through activation and the first bill, to money collected.

telco.why: Problems in an early step, such as a stuck order, appear later as a billing complaint, so agents trace the whole path.

nordwave.label: Fulfilment
nordwave.description: The part of the operator's process that delivers what was sold: checks the order, configures services, ships SIMs or devices and activates.

telco.why: It is one of the three standard process areas (fulfilment, assurance, billing). Orders that fail here are the fallout the operations team works on.

nordwave.label: Assurance
nordwave.description: The part of the operator's process that keeps service running: monitors faults and quality, finds causes and restores service.

telco.why: It is the source of outage news that Care needs: a customer complaint may be an already known network problem.

nordwave.label: Service order
nordwave.description: The technical instruction to set up or change a service on the network, created from the commercial product order.

telco.why: A product order can look complete while its service order has failed. Order status for the customer must use both.

nordwave.label: Service qualification
nordwave.description: Checking whether a service can be delivered at a given address or to a given device, before the customer orders.

telco.why: It prevents sales that cannot be delivered. Home-move and broadband journeys start here.

nordwave.label: Field service visit
nordwave.description: A scheduled visit by a technician to a customer's address, for an installation or a repair.

telco.why: Visits are expensive and customers plan around them. Agents offering one must check the address and available slots.

nordwave.label: SIM swap
nordwave.description: Moving a phone number to a new SIM or eSIM, for example after a loss, a new handset or fraud.

telco.why: SIM swap is a known route for account takeover, so identity checks must be applied before any agent starts one.

nordwave.label: Customer-facing service
nordwave.description: A service as the customer understands it, such as 'mobile data' or 'voicemail', built from technical services.

telco.why: It is the link between what is sold (product) and what runs on the network (resource-facing service). Agents explaining a fault stay at this level.

nordwave.label: Resource-facing service
nordwave.description: A technical service that uses network equipment or systems, such as a bearer, a number range or a profile on the core network.

telco.why: Faults happen at this level. A mapping from a customer's service to its resource-facing services is what lets a fault be traced to affected customers.

nordwave.label: Identity verification
nordwave.description: Proving that the person asking is the account holder, with a password, one-time code, document check or the SIM itself.

telco.why: No credit, SIM swap, port-out or address change should happen without it. Agents verify first and record how.

nordwave.label: Trouble to resolve
nordwave.description: The path from a customer reporting a problem, through diagnosis and repair, to confirmed resolution.

telco.why: It joins Care and Network: a ticket should carry the network fault so that the customer is told once and correctly.
kpis: tickets linked to a network fault

nordwave.label: Service level agreement
nordwave.description: A promise on service quality, such as availability, speed or repair time, with a remedy when it is missed.

telco.why: Business customers hold the operator to the SLA. When it is breached, a credit is due by contract and is no longer goodwill.

nordwave.label: Quality of service
nordwave.description: The measurable quality a user gets: speed, delay, lost packets and call quality. Different services are given different priorities.

telco.why: It is the technical side of 'my internet is slow'. Care should compare the customer's complaint with measured quality before blaming a device.

nordwave.label: Network slice
nordwave.description: A separate logical network on shared 5G infrastructure, with its own speed, delay and isolation guarantees.

telco.why: Slices let an operator sell guaranteed quality to a business. This is a new product type that the catalogue and the SLA must describe.

nordwave.label: Radio access network
nordwave.description: The masts, antennas and radio equipment that connect phones to the operator.

telco.why: Most coverage complaints and capacity limits are in the radio network, so it is the first place agents look for a local fault.

nordwave.label: Core network
nordwave.description: The central systems that authenticate users, set up sessions, route traffic and send usage and charging records.

telco.why: A fault here affects many customers at once. It also feeds the charging and usage records that billing uses.

nordwave.label: Consent
nordwave.description: The customer's permission to use their data or contact them for a stated purpose, which they can withdraw.

telco.why: An agent can only use data for a purpose the customer allowed. A retention offer sent to someone who opted out of marketing is a breach.

nordwave.label: Regulatory obligation
nordwave.description: A rule set by a regulator or law that the operator must follow, for example data roaming caps, number porting times and data protection.

telco.why: These rules override commercial policy. In the EU, for instance, a number must normally be ported within one working day, and a default cap protects roaming data.

nordwave.label: Approval gate
nordwave.description: A step where a named person must approve an action before it takes effect, usually above a value or risk limit.

telco.why: It is how an agent stays inside its authority: below the limit it acts, above it a person decides on the evidence.
